evidence.reason: The finding targets recover_publication, which at the current tip reads remote_head via `ls-remote` (line 734), then for an open PR leases the recovery push on that observed value (line 763) while only requiring it to be an ancestor of the prepared head (line 761: `if remote_head and not c.is_ancestor(remote_head, head)`). It never uses the journaled `publication['target']` as the lease and never asserts `remote_head == target`. If a maintainer resets the branch to an ancestor A and `pr_info` returns a stale `headRefOid == target` (passing the line 744 check), then A is accepted as a fast-forward base and `--force-with-lease=...:A` matches the ref still at A, so the push fast-forwards A->head and resurrects the commits the reset removed. This contradicts the code's own comment (lines 757-760) claiming "a maintainer reset to an ancestor cannot be silently resurrected by this push," so it is an implementation error in stated behavior, not merely a hardening request. Leasing `publication['target']` for the open-PR recovery push makes the push fail when the ref is not at the expected target while still succeeding when it is—a minimal, compatible fix that leaves the already-landed path (line 741) unchanged.
